--- title: "Series TR01: #01 Installing R and RStudio" author: "Dominik Schulz" date: "2026-04-23" sidebar: sidebarTR01 categories: [tutorial, programming, TR01] --- This entry marks the first post in the new Series **TR01: Setting up R**, which is supposed to guide the readers through the process of installing R and RStudio, of getting familiarized with the RStudio software interface, and of adjusting some basic global settings within the software. The start makes today's post on how to install R and RStudio. A data analyst's most important tool is their software (aside from their brains maybe), which does all of the wonderous and amazing numerical heavy-lifting. There are many different pieces of software like Python, SAS, SQL, and many more, each of them with their own specific strengths and purposes; however, a natural choice to dive into statistical analyses is the free program **R** alongside its integrated development environment (IDE) **RStudio**. The former is maintained by the R Core Team, whereas the latter is a (still free) corporate product by [Posit](https://posit.co/). While the program R itself is technically enough to do all the fancy analyses we wish to implement, RStudio makes employing the program much more intuitive. Firstly, we install R from the [website of the Comprehensive R Archive Network (CRAN)](https://cran.r-project.org/). ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Figure 1: The top of the CRAN webpage.](CRANpage.png){width=620} ::: ::: At the top of the webpage, there is a section called **Download and Install R**, which is where you need to pick the correct link in accordance with your computer's operating system. For example, for Windows users, you must follow **Download R for Windows** $\rightarrow$ **base** $\rightarrow$ **Download R-4.5.3 for Windows** (note that R-4.5.3 is the current version as of writing this post and may be replaced by an updated version at a later time point). This will start the download of a file **R-4.5.3-win.exe**. Run that file on your computer and follow the instructions and confirm until the installation is complete. For other operating systems, you need to follow the corresponding links on the CRAN website, e.g. **Download R for macOS** for laptops running macOS. Secondly, to install RStudio visit the corresponding [RStudio download page](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop) of Posit. The site reminds you, too, that you should first install R from CRAN. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Figure 2: The RStudio download page.](RStudioDownloadPage.png){width=625} ::: ::: Then it provides various RStudio download links for different operating systems. Once you have downloaded the correct one for your system (for example on Windows click the big button labelled **DOWNLOAD RSTUDIO DESKTOP FOR WINDOWS**), run the downloaded executable, follow the instructions showing up on your screen and confirm until the installation is complete. In the next entry to Series TR01, we will explain the basic RStudio program interface. Best,
Dominik
